svg.title: I'm not afraid of storms, for I'm learning how to sail my ship.

text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/10/27 - Quote - 01

svg.title: Storm clouds over the sea make Amy's sailing metaphor visible.

text.tspan: Storm clouds over the sea make Amy's sailing metaphor visible.
I'm not afraid of storms, for
I'm learning how to sail my
ship.
Amy March (fictional character) · Louisa May Alcott · Little Women, Part
Two, Chapter XLIV · Published 1869
Amy has returned to her family after marrying Laurie.
Her mother asks how married life is going. Amy
answers with the image of a ship. Life has been
pleasant so far, but she knows that difficulties may
come. She does not claim to know everything.
Instead, she says she is learning to manage her own
journey. Her confidence comes from practice, not
from expecting perfect weather.
Storms represent difficulties, and sailing represents
managing life. For means because here: learning
gives Amy a reason to feel less afraid.
Does Amy expect an easy life, or believe she can
learn to handle difficulties? Explain. (Model: She
believes she can learn to handle difficulties. The
storms may still come.)
